title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is a handwritten sheet on the back of a typescript (the neighbouring pages are typed SGA-style étale cohomology: purity and cycle class, Hochschild–Serre). The handwritten text is about the comparison between p-adic étale and crystalline realizations of motives, phrased in Tannakian language. Grothendieck called this problem the 'foncteur mystérieux' around 1970.

Step 1. There is a Tannakian category of motives, or of cohomological realizations. It has a p-adic étale fibre functor T_p, with group G, and base change gives G_K. There is also a crystalline fibre functor T_cr over K, presumably K = Frac W(k) or a field over it. Its values are first noted as 'graded and filtered vector spaces' (struck out), then simply as K-vector spaces.

Step 2. Two fibre functors over K differ by a torsor. Let Q be the G_K-torsor Isom^⊗((T_p)_K, T_cr). Then T_cr ≅ Q ∧^{G_K} (T_p)_K. The automorphism group of T_cr is the inner twist G'' = G_K^Q, i.e. Ad(Q)/Aut(Q). The comparison k_2 : G_K → G'' is well defined only up to conjugation. The struck-out lines 'définie modulo conj. par G''', 'U''(K)', 'torseur sous U''' show him trying to make this rigid.

Step 3. Over the field L where the variety and its de Rham cohomology live, T_cr ⊗_K L acquires the Hodge filtration (Berthelot–Ogus style identification with de Rham). There is an isomorphism of tensor functors gr(T_cr ⊗_K L) ≅ T_Hdg, the Hodge realization graded via a cocharacter/grading i_2.

Step 4. A filtration on a fibre functor is the same as a reduction of the structure group to a parabolic. So P (the stabilizer of the filtration) is a parabolic, and G' = G_L^P. The filtered isomorphisms give a torsor R under U' ⊂ G', the unipotent radical (margin: 'gp unipotent'). R embeds in Isom(Q_L, P) and is defined by j_2. Note G'' ⊃ U''.

Step 5. Finally there is a Frobenius on T_cr, a σ-semilinear isomorphism F : T_DR^σ ≅ T_DR.

So the data being assembled is a G-torsor with a parabolic reduction (Hodge filtration), its Levi quotient (Hodge grading) and a σ-linear Frobenius. This is a Tannakian, motivic-Galois-group version of a filtered F-isocrystal with G-structure. The aim is to describe T_p (the Galois representation) in terms of this structure, i.e. the mysterious functor.
errors: k_2 : G_K → G'' is not canonical. It is an isomorphism only after trivializing Q, and is defined up to inner automorphisms; the struck-out text shows Grothendieck noticed this. The exact meaning of 'G_K^Q / Ad(Q)' (probably '= Ad(Q)') is unclear.
The Frobenius F : T^σ → T is an isomorphism only after inverting p (isocrystal), not integrally.
The statement gr(T_cr⊗L) ≅ T_Hdg presupposes the crystalline–de Rham comparison and Hodge–de Rham degeneration; it is taken for granted here.
The page does not say how R and the U''-torsor are related; the struck-out note 'il faudra expliciter...' leaves this open. The construction is unfinished.

ideas.what: Comparison of étale and crystalline fibre functors as a torsor Q under the motivic/Tannakian group, with T_cr = Q ∧ T_p and an inner-twisted automorphism group
ideas.modern_name: p-adic period torsor (Tannakian form of Fontaine's comparison; torsor of comparison isomorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine (period rings, 1979–82); Tannakian torsor viewpoint Saavedra Rivano 1972, Deligne 1982/1990
ideas.where_published: The mysterious functor is mentioned in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 talk 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux'; a Tannakian torsor formulation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Filtration on a fibre functor as reduction to a parabolic, with gr equal to the Hodge fibre functor and a torsor under the unipotent radical
ideas.modern_name: Filtered fibre functors (Saavedra, Ziegler), parabolic reduction via cocharacters (Hodge cocharacter μ)

ideas.what: Combining a G-torsor, Hodge filtration (parabolic) and σ-linear Frobenius

missed.claim: An early, apparently unpublished Tannakian formulation of the 'mysterious functor'. The crystalline realization is encoded as a torsor under the motivic group, with a parabolic reduction from the Hodge filtration and a Frobenius. This anticipates the G-structure viewpoint on filtered isocrystals (Kottwitz, Rapoport–Richartz).
missed.quote: Q torseur sous G_K ; T_cr ≃ Q ∧^{G_K} (T_p)_K ; un torseur R sous U' ⊂ G' = G_L^P ; il y a sur le foncteur T_cr un Frobenius F : T_DR^σ ≅ T_DR
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically it shows Grothendieck around 1970 already thinking of p-adic Hodge comparison in torsor/group-theoretic terms, not only for vector spaces. Mathematically it is subsumed by later theory; its interest is mainly priority and history.

deep.surprise_reason: A fragmentary but clear early Tannakian/G-structure framing of the crystalline–étale comparison (torsor, parabolic from the filtration, unipotent torsor, Frobenius). It predates Fontaine and Rapoport–Richartz, but it is unfinished and the overall program (the mysterious functor) is known to be Grothendieck's.
transcription_corrections: 'G'' = G_K^Q / Ad(Q)' probably reads 'G'' = G_K^Q = Ad(Q)' (twisted group identified with the adjoint/automorphism group of Q).
Left margin note near U' ⊂ G' reads approximately 'gp unipotent' (U' is the unipotent radical).
The right margin contains a crossed-out note ('il faudra expliciter que cela correspond à ... i_2 ... ci-dessus'), correctly marked as deleted.
The last line likely reads 'T_cr un Frobenius', with the subscript partially overwritten; the formula is F : T_DR^σ ⥲ T_DR (σ-twist written as superscript ~/σ).
